description: Write the standard for beginner-friendly Livebook docs. Include: self-contained Mix.install setup, credential cell, Logger.configure(level: :warning), Jido.start() + Jido.start_agent(Jido.default_instance(), ...), stable public APIs only in the main path, one success path first, inspection second, advanced internals moved out of the critical path, and expectations for livebook metadata plus drift tests.

comments.text:
Proposed canonical beginner Livebook pattern:

1. The notebook must be self-contained. Do not require readers to complete another guide before they can run it.
2. Start with Mix.install, provider key setup, and Logger.configure(level: :warning).
3. Use Jido.start() for the default runtime in Livebook and start agents with Jido.start_agent(Jido.default_instance(), ...).
4. Use stable public APIs only in the main path: ask/3, await/2, ask_sync/3, and Jido.AgentServer.status/1 for inspection.
5. Show one success path first, then one inspection/debugging path.
6. Keep lifecycle hooks, strategy command atoms, request transformers, LiveView wiring, and other internals out of the critical path; move them to advanced sections or separate docs.
7. Runnable notebooks should include consistent livebook metadata and a matching drift test under test/livebooks/docs.

Applied to AI chat specifically: the main path should be one agent pid, two turns on that same pid, and an inspection of status.snapshot.details.conversation to prove multi-turn context works before showing any customization hooks.

title: Define the canonical Livebook tutorial pattern and author checklist
